description:
Bug in src/fetcher/crest_http_client.cr resolve_redirect_url (lines ~292-307):

  ```crystal
  rescue ex
    if ex.is_a?(URI::Error)
      raise ex
    else
      raise URI::Error.new(\"Invalid redirect URL: #{redirect_url}\")
    end
  end
  ```

  The outer `rescue ex` (no class qualifier) catches Exception. The
  inner `if ex.is_a?(URI::Error)` re-raises it. The else branch raises
  a fresh URI::Error.

  In Crystal, `rescue` without a class catches StandardError, not
  Exception. URI::Error is a StandardError subclass, so this works at
  runtime, but the if/else is misleading: any non-URI::Error that
  bubbles up (ArgumentError, etc.) gets converted to URI::Error,
  losing the original type and message.

  Also, the if-branch is reachable only if the URI::Error is raised
  after the begin block - but `URI.parse` already raises URI::Error
  directly, and the only other URI operation is `base.resolve(relative)`
  which also raises URI::Error. The else branch is the only one that
  ever runs in practice (when something like ArgumentError is raised
  by String#starts_with? or by Address parsing, which doesn't happen
  here).

  Net effect: the code is *almost* equivalent to:

  ```crystal
  rescue ex : URI::Error
    raise ex
  rescue
    raise URI::Error.new(\"Invalid redirect URL: #{redirect_url}\")
  ```

  ...which would be clearer.

Fix:

  Replace with the cleaner form, or simply:

  ```crystal
  rescue ex : URI::Error
    raise ex
  rescue
    raise URI::Error.new(\"Invalid redirect URL: #{redirect_url}\")
  end
  ```

  If this gets folded into the RedirectPolicy extraction ticket, the
  fix is part of the move. If the extraction is deferred, ship this
  as a follow-up.

Test: a redirect target like \"http://example.com/path with spaces\"
should raise URI::Error, not ArgumentError or some other intermediate
type. Add a regression test in spec/crest_http_client_redirect_spec.cr.
title: Fix resolve_redirect_url dead-branch in rescue
